queue_items.claim: The row's sole front-seam signal, a first-person resolve onset, does not discriminate the seam and is neither spliced nor disclosed as continuous across it.
queue_items.grounds: The row opens 'A first-person resolve opens the unit' and records oracle_frame.first_person_resolve_onset as its only observed signal, but the first-person-singular voice is already running in the immediately preceding verses: שׂ֧וֹשׂ אָשִׂ֣ישׂ בַּֽיהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.61.10, byte tier) with נַפְשִׁי֙ and בֵּֽאלֹהַ֔י (oshb:Isa.61.10, byte tier). The book-order neighbor row states this explicitly for the same seam ('the first-person-singular voice itself runs on unbroken ... rather than by any change in speaker or person'); this row discloses no cross-seam continuity at its own front seam. The resolve itself is also never spliced — the only Hebrew given at that verse, צִדְקָ֔הּ וִישׁוּעָתָ֖הּ (oshb:Isa.62.1, byte tier), is the third-person Zion phrase from the verse's second half, while the resolve verbs לֹ֣א אֶחֱשֶׁ֔ה and לֹ֣א אֶשְׁק֑וֹט (oshb:Isa.62.1, byte tier) are absent from the row.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair (no seam movement): splice לֹ֣א אֶחֱשֶׁ֔ה and לֹ֣א אֶשְׁק֑וֹט (oshb:Isa.62.1, byte tier) as the named onset, disclose that the first-person-singular voice straddles the front seam from oshb:Isa.61.10, and re-state what actually discriminates the seam (the lamed-purpose Zion/Jerusalem vow) — observed_substrate_signals and confidence are dependent fields of that restatement.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: A first-person resolve opens the unit; Zion is named in the third person, “until her righteousness shines out like the dawn, and her salvation like a burning lamp.” (web:Isa.62.1), matching צִדְקָ֔הּ וִישׁוּעָתָ֖הּ (oshb:Isa.62.1, byte tier). The direct second-person address to Zion begins at the following verse, “The nations will see your righteousness” (web:Isa.62.2), and runs through the renaming and marriage imagery to this unit's own close, “As a bridegroom rejoices over his bride, so your God will rejoice over you.” (web:Isa.62.5). Isa.62.6 introduces a new participant group, the posted watchmen, “I have set watchmen on your walls, Jerusalem.” (web:Isa.62.6), matching שֹֽׁמְרִ֔ים (oshb:Isa.62.6, byte tier), and the speaker's own first-person act shifts from the vow of Isa.62.1 to an act of appointment already completed; the second-person-feminine-singular addressee and the first-person voice both continue unbroken past this seam, so the seam is marked by the new watchmen and the shift from vow to appointment, not by any change of addressee, speaker, or person, closing this unit.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending the unit through Isa.62.6's watchmen scene was rejected because that verse introduces a new participant group, the posted watchmen, and turns the speaker's own first-person act from the vow opening this unit to an act of appointment already completed; the second-person-feminine-singular addressee and the first-person voice both continue unbroken across that seam, so the boundary rests on the new participant group and the vow-to-appointment shift, not on any vocative or change of speaker.
shipped_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
shipped_row.device_notes: No parashah mark falls at the front seam (oshb:Isa.61.11) or inside Isa.62.1-Isa.62.5. Isa.62.3 stages both the ketiv and qere forms of the diadem noun side by side, וצנוף וּצְנִ֥יף (oshb:Isa.62.3, byte tier) — 'and a diadem' — read either way.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: A new first-person voice opens with rejoicing, “I will greatly rejoice in Yahweh! My soul will be joyful in my God,” (web:Isa.61.10), matching שׂ֧וֹשׂ אָשִׂ֣ישׂ בַּֽיהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.61.10, byte tier), sharing no stated referent with the third-person 'offspring' of the immediately preceding report. The bridegroom-and-bride simile carries the same voice through a comparison to Adonai Yahweh's own action, “so the Lord Yahweh will cause righteousness and praise to spring up before all the nations.” (web:Isa.61.11), matching אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה (oshb:Isa.61.11, byte tier). Isa.62.1 opens a distinct first-person resolve, “For Zion's sake I will not hold my peace, and for Jerusalem's sake I will not rest,” (web:Isa.62.1); the first-person-singular voice itself runs on unbroken from this unit's own opening rejoicing into that vow, so the seam is marked by the shift in rhetorical mode — from a sung report of what Yahweh has already done to a vow of what the speaker will now do — rather than by any change in speaker or person, closing this unit.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating Isa.61.10-Isa.61.11 as a continuation of the restoration promise closing at Isa.61.9 was rejected because the abrupt shift from third-person description of 'their offspring' to a first-person 'I will greatly rejoice' introduces a new speaking voice without a stated referent.
prev_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
prev_row.device_notes: A setumah (single-witness) at oshb:Isa.61.9 marks the front seam immediately before this unit opens; a paseq (single-witness, count-only, no intra-verse position asserted) sits at oshb:Isa.61.11, inside this unit's own close. This unit's own opening simile reuses, at accent_stripped tier, the garland word that closes the anointed speaker's commission three verses earlier: פְּאֵ֜ר (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier) against פְּאֵ֔ר (oshb:Isa.61.10, byte tier) differ only in cantillation; the standalone token stands in exactly 2 verses book-wide. This is disclosed continuity across this unit's own front seam, and it does not resolve whether the rejoicing voice is the same figure who speaks beginning at Isa.61.1. Labeling this two-verse unit hymn_doxology extends the operative category beyond the strategy's own enumerated song sites, by the sung first-person praise content of its own bytes; the speaking voice — Zion personified, or the same figure who speaks beginning at Isa.61.1 — is left open rather than decided here.

next_row.boundary_rationale: An explicit vocative and a new first-person divine act open the unit, “I have set watchmen on your walls, Jerusalem.” (web:Isa.62.6), matching עַל חוֹמֹתַ֣יִךְ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם הִפְקַ֨דְתִּי֙ שֹֽׁמְרִ֔ים (oshb:Isa.62.6, byte tier). The speaker charges those watchmen, in second-person-plural imperatives addressed to them, to give Yahweh no rest, אַל דֳּמִ֖י לָכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.62.6, byte tier) and וְאַֽל תִּתְּנ֥וּ (oshb:Isa.62.7, byte tier); that charge is answered by an oath formula, “Yahweh has sworn by his right hand, and by the arm of his strength,” (web:Isa.62.8), matching נִשְׁבַּ֧ע יְהוָ֛ה (oshb:Isa.62.8, byte tier), that introduces Yahweh's own quoted promise through the unit's close, “Those who have gathered it will drink it in the courts of my sanctuary.” (web:Isa.62.9). Isa.62.10 opens a fresh plural-imperative summons, “Go through, go through the gates!” (web:Isa.62.10), addressed to an unnamed group rather than continuing the charge just laid on the watchmen, marking this unit's close.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at Isa.62.8's oath formula was rejected because the sworn content answers the charge the speaker lays on the watchmen at Isa.62.6-Isa.62.7 without a change of addressee or scene.

queue_items.claim: The front-seam driver is a vocative in apposition to an addressee that runs on unbroken across the seam, and that continuity is undisclosed in this row.
queue_items.grounds: The row argues 'An explicit vocative and a new first-person divine act open the unit'. The vocative stands as the third token of MT 62:6, עַל חוֹמֹתַ֣יִךְ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם (oshb:Isa.62.6, byte tier), in apposition to a second-person-feminine-singular addressee already running from MT 62:2 — צִדְקֵ֔ךְ and כְּבוֹדֵ֑ךְ (oshb:Isa.62.2, byte tier) — through עָלַ֖יִךְ (oshb:Isa.62.5, byte tier) at the preceding unit's own close. It therefore names the same addressee rather than opening a fresh one, and the book-order neighbor row argues this same seam as marked 'not by any change of addressee, speaker, or person'. This row discloses addressee alternation inside its span but not the unbroken address across its own front seam.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair (no seam movement): disclose that the second-person-feminine-singular address straddles the front seam from MT 62:2 onward, and re-state the onset as a vocative re-address plus a new completed first-person divine act rather than as a fresh vocative addressee; observed_substrate_signals and confidence are dependent fields.

queue_items.claim: The rear seam at 62:9 | 62:10 is argued on exactly the ground the book-order neighbor row rejects for the same seam.
queue_items.grounds: This row closes because 'Isa.62.10 opens a fresh plural-imperative summons ... addressed to an unnamed group rather than continuing the charge just laid on the watchmen'. The neighbor row opening at 62:10 rejects that ground in terms: 'The preceding verses already command an addressed-plural group, the posted watchmen; the turn at this unit's own onset is not a shift to an unnamed addressee but a shift in content', and its rejected_alternative repeats 'not because it addresses an unnamed group'. The bytes support the neighbor: MT 62:6-62:7 already charge a plural addressee at אַל דֳּמִ֖י לָכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.62.6, byte tier) and וְאַֽל תִּתְּנ֥וּ (oshb:Isa.62.7, byte tier), so the addressee of the summons is no more unnamed at 62:10 than at 62:6.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair (no seam movement): re-argue the rear seam on the verse-initial doubled imperative and the content turn to highway preparation, dropping the 'unnamed group' ground so the seam is argued compatibly from both sides.

queue_items.grounds: The row calls 62:10 'a fresh plural-imperative summons' and cites only web:Isa.62.10; the Hebrew that carries the claim, עִבְר֤וּ עִבְרוּ֙ בַּשְּׁעָרִ֔ים (oshb:Isa.62.10, byte tier), is never spliced and oshb:Isa.62.10 is absent from boundary_evidence_refs, which pairs an oshb ref with every other web ref it cites. The claim is byte-true, and the book-order neighbor row splices exactly this run at byte tier for the same seam.

Prepare the way of the people!” (web:Isa.62.10), matching עִבְר֤וּ עִבְרוּ֙ בַּשְּׁעָרִ֔ים (oshb:Isa.62.10, byte tier). The unit closes on a renaming formula, “They will call them “The Holy People, Yahweh's Redeemed”.” (web:Isa.62.12), matching עַם הַקֹּ֖דֶשׁ גְּאוּלֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Isa.62.12, byte tier). This renaming pair brackets the naming clause “You will be called by a new name” (web:Isa.62.2), matching וְקֹ֤רָא לָךְ֙ שֵׁ֣ם חָדָ֔שׁ (oshb:Isa.62.2, byte tier), together with the renaming “you will be called Hephzibah” (web:Isa.62.4), matching יִקָּרֵא֙ (oshb:Isa.62.4, byte tier); the recurring niphal form itself, יִקָּרֵא֙ (oshb:Isa.62.4) and יִקָּרֵ֣א (oshb:Isa.62.12), is identical at accent_stripped tier and differs only in cantillation. queue_items.claim: The rear-seam warrant is byte-false: MT 63:7 does not open a first-person-plural recital, and no change of grammatical person occurs across the seam.
queue_items.grounds: The row ends its span 'because 63:7 pivots to a different speaker and a different speech-act: a first-person-plural recital of Yahweh's mercies replaces the divine warrior's own first-person report'. MT 63:7's speech-act verb is first-person SINGULAR: חַֽסְדֵ֨י יְהוָ֤ה אַזְכִּיר֙ (oshb:Isa.63.7, byte tier), matched by the English witness's 'I will tell of the loving kindnesses of Yahweh' (web:Isa.63.7); the verse's only plural first-person element is the object suffix on גְּמָלָ֖נוּ (oshb:Isa.63.7, byte tier). The preceding unit closes in first-person singular as well — וְאָב֤וּס עַמִּים֙ בְּאַפִּ֔י (oshb:Isa.63.6, byte tier) — so the person is unchanged across the seam. The book-order neighbor row states this correctly and oppositely ('a first-person-singular self-announcing speech-act verb ... the same grammatical person as the preceding unit's own divine-warrior voice, so the seam is marked by the change in speech-act, not by any change of person'). The row also carries no oshb:Isa.63.7 entry and no splice for the verse its rear seam turns on, and ships at confidence 'high' with frontier_flag_considered false.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair (no seam movement; the seam itself survives on the speech-act change and the tier-3 SAMEKH already disclosed at MT 63:6): delete the 'first-person-plural recital' ground, re-argue the seam as a change of speech-act at unchanged grammatical person, splice חַֽסְדֵ֨י יְהוָ֤ה אַזְכִּיר֙ (oshb:Isa.63.7, byte tier), add oshb:Isa.63.7 to boundary_evidence_refs, and re-test confidence and frontier_flag now that the person-shift ground is withdrawn.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: This unit is bounded by a dramatic question-and-answer frame: the prophetic voice opens with a verse-initial interrogative, מִי זֶ֣ה בָּ֣א מֵאֱד֗וֹם (oshb:Isa.63.1, byte tier), “Who is this who comes from Edom” (web:Isa.63.1); the clause that follows opens instead on a bare demonstrative, זֶ֚ה הָד֣וּר בִּלְבוּשׁ֔וֹ (oshb:Isa.63.1, byte tier), rendered as a second question, “Who is this who is glorious in his clothing,” only in the English witness. The challenged figure answers in the first person, closing that reply with "אֲנִ֛י מְדַבֵּ֥ר בִּצְדָקָ֖ה רַ֥ב לְהוֹשִֽׁיעַ" (oshb:Isa.63.1, byte tier) ('I who speak in righteousness, mighty to save'). A further verse-initial interrogative opens the next verse, מַדּ֥וּעַ (oshb:Isa.63.2, byte tier), “Why is your clothing red” (web:Isa.63.2), continuing the exchange. The same first-person divine-warrior voice continues in unbroken speech through the vengeance-and-treading report, closing the unit at “I poured their lifeblood out on the earth.” (web:Isa.63.6). The unit ends there because 63:7 pivots to a different speaker and a different speech-act: a first-person-plural recital of Yahweh's mercies replaces the divine warrior's own first-person report, with no further interrogative sustaining the dialogue frame.

The petition runs through the single MT verse that spans two WEB verses: the never-ruled complaint "הָיִ֗ינוּ מֵֽעוֹלָם֙ לֹֽא מָשַׁ֣לְתָּ בָּ֔ם לֹֽא נִקְרָ֥א שִׁמְךָ֖ עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם" (oshb:Isa.63.19, byte tier) lives at web:Isa.63.19 ('we have become like those from of old you never ruled, your name not called upon them'), and the same MT verse's tear-the-heavens plea "לוּא קָרַ֤עְתָּ שָׁמַ֨יִם֙ יָרַ֔דְתָּ מִפָּנֶ֖יךָ הָרִ֥ים נָזֹֽלּוּ" (oshb:Isa.63.19, byte tier) lives at web:Isa.64.1 ('oh that you would tear the heavens, you would come down, the mountains would quake'); both halves belong to this row because they are one Hebrew sentence sharing one verse's bytes, and a row boundary is not argued between them. The theophany imagery continues past the split (fire kindling brushwood, the nations trembling, mountains quaking again at 64:2-3) and the unit closes at the affirmation "לֹֽא רָאָ֗תָה אֱלֹהִים֙ זוּלָ֣תְךָ֔" (oshb:Isa.64.3, byte tier) (web:Isa.64.4, 'the eye has not seen a God besides you'), immediately before the confessional turn “Behold, you were angry, and we sinned.” (web:Isa.64.5) opens a different speech-act.

Don't remember iniquity forever.” (web:Isa.64.9), reporting the ruined holy cities and temple (web:Isa.64.10 = oshb:Isa.64.9 through web:Isa.64.11 = oshb:Isa.64.10) before closing on a final unanswered double question, “Will you hold yourself back for these things, Yahweh?
